title: My cybersecurity and cloud learning goal

claim_boundary.statement: I am publishing a learning intention and an evidence route. I am not claiming completion, mastery, a credential or professional experience.
claim_boundary.safe_scope: I will use the fictional or dummy evidence and the safe boundaries stated in each lab.
claim_boundary.tool_limit: A matching helper result can check an expected decision or format; it cannot judge my reasoning or prove independent skill.

status_model.planned: I have selected the lab and its prerequisites, but I have not claimed an attempt.
status_model.guided: I have worked with instructions, examples or prompts and recorded that help.
status_model.solo: I have preserved a first answer to a changed case before checking a reference.
status_model.reviewed: A person has challenged my evidence and reasoning, and I have retained the feedback and correction.
status_model.recall: I have tried different facts later without reusing my earlier answer.

review_gate.statement: Before I start a dependent lab, I will keep reviewed or equivalent evidence for each named dependency.
review_gate.unavailable_reviewer: I will mark the work awaiting review and will not call it independently demonstrated.

labs.title: Use shell commands for read-only troubleshooting

evidence.artifact: I will retain my first decisions, the supplied fictional command notebook and a worksheet citing each record ID, shell, working directory, actual arguments, match, error and status fields, pipeline-stage statuses, byte margin, service state, process and expected PIDs, listener bind, port and owner fields, uncertainty and smallest next read-only check.
evidence.decision: I will use only the supplied fictional command notebook for this planned route; its commands and result fields are transcriptions, and the helper reads JSON but does not execute commands or inspect a host. I will apply the stated lexical path and status rules: actual argument tokens and the working directory support only the bounded path result, not links, permissions or a live file check; grep, PowerShell and pipeline statuses must be tied to the named command and captured fields, and an empty result differs from an error; and the byte result tests only the stated budget. A supplied service state does not establish the expected state or cause; a PID and process-name match does not establish identity or intent and may change; and a loopback or wildcard listener and owner PID do not establish remote reachability. The optional Linux and Windows live lanes were not run during package authoring and will remain unperformed unless I retain separate live evidence. I will not elevate privileges, install tools, change or start or stop a service, or scan a remote system. A helper or reference match will not prove live command execution, host state, safety, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a synthetic DNS cache worksheet that cites each query ID, owner and record type, CNAME path, receipt and query times, TTL or negative-cache lifetime, expiry arithmetic, seconds remaining, predicted answer, uncertainty and next check.

I will calculate remaining life as `max(0, receipt time + TTL − query time)`, treat zero as refresh-required, require every CNAME and final record in a chain to remain fresh, and use the smaller of SOA TTL and MINIMUM for a negative entry. I will distinguish exact-name NXDOMAIN from type-specific NODATA and treat missing or expired cache evidence as refresh-required, not proof that a name or service is unavailable. labs.title: Review VPN routes and DNS scope

evidence.artifact: I will retain synthetic before-and-after route maps and a separate DNS-path table citing each row ID, destination or name, address family, selected prefix or suffix rule, metric, resolver address, before-and-after path, stated intent, result, uncertainty and next check. I will keep the optional VM comparison and any live path or query test explicitly marked unperformed and separate from the supplied evidence.
evidence.decision: I will use only the supplied offline snapshots. For each traffic destination, I will select the longest matching prefix in its address family and use the lowest metric only between equally specific routes. For each name query, I will select the most specific whole-name or dot-boundary suffix rule and route every selected resolver address using the same route rule. I will keep IPv4 and IPv6 separate and compare each after-path with the stated local or tunnel intent; no route, no resolver, a different path or mixed resolver paths will not meet that intent. I will not connect a VPN, issue DNS requests or change routes or resolver settings. A selected path does not establish that a tunnel connected, traffic was encrypted, a resolver answered or a destination was reachable. Policy and source routing, multiple tables, equal-cost routing, interface-bound or application-specific DNS, fallback and cache behaviour, and tunnel transport remain outside this model. I will not treat helper or reference matches as evidence of completion, mastery, independent assessment or professional use.

labs.title: Capture and explain your own traffic

evidence.artifact: I will retain my own controlled loopback PCAP, exact capture and display filters, generator setup and logs, and a worksheet citing actual frame and TCP-stream numbers for one HTTP 200, one HTTP 404 and one failed connection.
evidence.decision: I will confirm capture permission and existing loopback support, then use only the lab’s `127.0.0.1` service and generated ports. I will start capture before the requests and use visible frames to distinguish a TCP connection, an HTTP 200, an HTTP 404 and a refused or timed-out connection. The generator and maintainer tests create local traffic and logs, not a PCAP, and no fixture or fixed answer will substitute for run-specific frame and stream references. Until I retain those references, I will mark capture pending and claim no Wireshark attempt. Missing packets will not prove firewall blocking, packet loss or server fault; a handshake will not prove application success; and a toy response will not prove a real business outcome. I will send no external traffic, install no software or change firewall or VM settings, and I will not treat generated or test results as proof of completion, mastery, independent assessment or professional use.

evidence.artifact: I will retain my first decisions, the supplied synthetic packet summaries and a marked DHCP/ARP exchange table citing each query ID; matching and excluded frames; client MAC and transaction ID; current, offered and requested addresses; server, destination and lease fields; ARP requester, target and claimed mapping; exchange and lease-link labels; uncertainty, help, correction and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only supplied fictional packet summaries from one stated observation point; I will not treat them as a real capture or send traffic. For DHCP, I will match both client MAC and transaction ID, read the Request fields to distinguish an initial allocation from a renewal, preserve message order and gaps, compare the expected server with the observed ACK or NAK and, for an ACK, compare the expected address. For ARP, I will match the requester IP and MAC and sought IP, require a reply addressed to that requester, keep replies without an earlier request separate, and report conflicting claimed MACs without assigning cause. I will link a lease to address use only when a matched Request and ACK precede an ARP request from the same client MAC using the acknowledged address. I will keep an absent message distinct from an event that did not happen, because the capture window or position may omit it and a renewal need not repeat Discover and Offer. I will not infer identity, address ownership, current lease validity, connectivity, server trust, malicious activity or root cause. I will keep relays, rebinding, other DHCP states, retransmissions, multiple offers, ARP probes and announcements outside this model. I will leave the optional comparison with separately approved saved evidence unperformed unless I retain separate run-specific records. I will treat a matching label as bounded consistency in the supplied summaries only, not as professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment. I will treat the stated one-observation-point scope, query grouping and related_dhcp links as supplied model assertions, and I will state that the helper neither discovers their provenance nor verifies it. I will use client MAC plus transaction ID only as this bounded model’s match and will omit DHCP client identifiers and chaddr variants. I will keep the model IPv4-only and leave IPv6 Neighbor Discovery outside scope. I will not treat frame order as elapsed time or an ACK as proof of receipt, acceptance, configuration or current lease validity; I will treat a later ARP request with the same MAC and IP as correlation only, not causation; and I will treat an ARP mapping as a claim, not proof of ownership or identity. I will leave the optional saved-evidence viewer lane unrun and, if it is separately approved later, I will require a disconnected environment with external name resolution disabled.

labs.title: Identify file types beyond the extension

evidence.artifact: I will retain my first prediction and decisions, the supplied synthetic case, notes, the practical receipt, the source and copied dummy files, and a file-type worksheet citing each item ID, filename and extension, reported MIME label, total size, inspected prefix length and hexadecimal bytes, source-before, source-after and copied-file SHA-256 values, the source-unchanged result, signature decision, alternative explanation, uncertainty and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only the package’s supplied synthetic cases and bounded local operation: create harmless PNG bytes, a tiny made-up SQLite database, plain text or short byte samples in a fresh lab folder; copy and hash them; inspect only their size and up to the first 16 bytes; and execute no sample. I will check zero length first, then require the complete eight-byte PNG signature or complete 16-byte SQLite signature; treat filename extensions and reported MIME labels as labels rather than proof; and leave incomplete or unsupported signatures type-undetermined. I will keep the fictional worksheet separate from the practical receipt and treat matching source hashes only as evidence that the source bytes stayed unchanged, not that metadata stayed unchanged or that a copy is safe. A signature match is only a format clue, and an extension mismatch does not establish malware or whole-file validity. Only PNG and SQLite signatures are recognized. I will use no personal file, device or browser profile and run no antivirus, full format validator or executable analysis. The saved package checks and practical receipts are maintainer evidence, not evidence that I performed the task. A helper or reference match, unit test or hash result will not establish factual completeness, a real file’s safety, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

Matching hashes support byte equality only at the recorded checks, and a matching source hash supports only that the source bytes stayed unchanged; neither establishes unchanged metadata, file safety, who performed an action, when an action occurred, or why a timestamp has a value. File times can be copied or set explicitly, and filesystem, operating-system, access-time, birth-time, timestamp-precision, cross-filesystem and clock behavior remain outside this single local experiment unless separately tested. I will use no personal file, coursework, disk, device or browser profile and will make no claim of real forensic acquisition, factual completeness, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment. A reference match, unit test, hash result or saved maintainer receipt will establish only bounded package behavior or recorded byte identity, not my performance or a real-world conclusion.

labs.title: Recover a deleted dummy file from a disposable image

evidence.artifact: I will retain my first prediction and decisions, the supplied synthetic case and notes, the practical receipt, the generated source image, read-only working copy, recovery log and separately extracted candidate when one is produced, plus a deleted-file-recovery worksheet citing the item ID, generated 32 KiB FAT12 geometry, directory-entry state and `0xe5` marker, FAT-copy agreement, cluster and allocation state, declared and candidate byte counts, known-file and extracted-candidate SHA-256 values, source-before and source-after hashes, decision, alternative explanation, uncertainty and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only the package’s supplied synthetic scenarios and bounded local operation in a fresh folder under this lab’s `run/` directory: construct the generated 32 KiB FAT12 layout in memory, write it only as a new ordinary image file, model deletion of one training entry and release of its cluster, reopen the working copy read-only, and extract at most one supported one-cluster candidate into a separate output folder. I will never mount the image or supply a device, personal file, coursework, browser profile or other external evidence. I will require the exact training geometry and agreeing FAT copies; distinguish an absent directory candidate from an allocated cluster or file larger than 512 bytes; compare candidate length with declared size before comparing SHA-256; and call a match only when both size and hash equal the known training file. I will keep the fictional worksheet separate from the actual local receipt and treat matching source hashes only as evidence that the source bytes stayed unchanged at the recorded checks, not that metadata stayed unchanged. An `0xe5` entry, free cluster or extracted byte sequence does not establish original provenance, who deleted a file, when or why deletion occurred, or complete recovery of arbitrary media. A known-file match establishes only byte equality for this generated training item. Missing or differing bytes do not prove that all prior data is gone or explain the difference. Mounting, recovery suites, fragmented files, physical disks, TRIM and damaged media remain untested. Reference matches, unit tests, hashes and maintainer receipts establish only bounded package behavior or recorded byte identity; they do not prove my performance, factual completeness, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

labs.title: Resolve a disagreement between two evidence sources

evidence.artifact: I will retain my first prediction and decisions, the supplied synthetic case, my notes, the practical receipt, the dummy source register and working copy, and the generated CSV timeline, plus a cross-source worksheet citing each pair, record and source ID; source kind and supplied collection note; observed and corrected UTC time; supplied clock error and uncertainty in seconds; request ID; recorded `object_sha256` value; corrected separation and combined uncertainty; exact decision label; source-register SHA-256 values before and after; byte-unchanged result; alternative explanation; uncertainty; next check; correction and help used.
evidence.decision: I will use only the package’s three supplied synthetic JSON scenarios and its bounded Python standard-library helper in a fresh `run/` folder. The helper copies and hashes a made-up source register and writes a CSV from its fields; it does not acquire endpoint, web or packet logs, inspect a real device or profile, use the network, or operate an external forensic tool. For each proposed pair of records from different supplied sources, I will calculate corrected time as observed UTC minus the supplied clock error, leave a null correction unresolved, and treat the intervals as touching or overlapping when corrected separation is no greater than the sum of the two supplied uncertainties. I will apply the first matching rule in order: two present request IDs that differ are `identifiers-conflict`; otherwise differing recorded object SHA-256 values are `content-conflict`; otherwise a missing request ID is `insufficient-link`; otherwise an unknown clock error is `clock-unresolved`; otherwise a separation greater than combined uncertainty is `time-conflict`; otherwise the result is `link-supported-within-clock-bounds`. I will retain the computed observation even when an earlier rule decides the label. I will treat request IDs, recorded object hashes, clock errors, uncertainty values and collection notes as supplied training fields. The practical before-and-after hash covers the dummy source-register bytes only; it does not recompute the recorded object hashes, verify metadata, provenance or source completeness, identify a person, or establish causation. A matching ID, recorded hash and compatible interval support only a proposed link within this fictional model; identifiers and logs can be missing, reused, copied, incomplete or wrong. The supplied challenge can be a solo attempt, but it is not a reviewer-prepared fresh unseen assessment. Package tests, shipped references, maintainer receipts or a matching answer establish only bounded package behavior or recorded byte equality, not that I ran the task, the quality of my reasoning, factual completeness, professional tool use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.
